threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still avoid walking through London Fields after dark, clutching your keys like a dagger. The rest of us just stroll through without a second thought.
Last night on the 47, a guy serenaded the entire bus with his guitar, only to get off at the next stop and leave us all stunned.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I heard a neighbor yelling about the BVG strike while watering their plants. Only in Neukölln do we mix protest with gardening.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop run by a retired opera singer offering free concerts on Fridays. The blend of flavors and notes is unbeatable.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they know which taco trucks keep their meat fresh at the Sunday farmers' market—always the ones with the longest lines.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a woman in the Muni shelter meticulously folding hundreds of origami cranes while waiting for the 47. Total peace in the chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals are drinking vermut at 1 PM. Most of us are just trying to catch the bus on time. It's not a party here, just life.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their confusion over La Rambla—staring at their map while walking in circles, missing the local side streets.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 149 is a reasonable route to get anywhere. The locals know the 38 is your best bet for avoiding a two-hour trek.
Last week on the 35, I saw a bloke trying to impress a girl by doing magic tricks. Half the bus was in stitches while he fumbled with a pack of cards.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: One night, I heard a group of kids arguing over whose turn it was to pick the Berlin currywurst spot. That's when I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find open-air clubs like Sisyphos, where partygoers dance through the night and into the next day, often with dogs in tow.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they instinctively move away from the curb as a BART train rattles overhead, no matter how busy the street is.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni in the Tenderloin where a guy was rapping about the 19 bus like it was a love letter. Only in SF do the routes inspire such passion.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can grab a café con leche and sit for hours, but in Gràcia, you’ll get side-eye if you hog a table during the busy evening rush.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by how they stand at the corner of Carrer del Bisbe, taking photos of anything that moves—especially the pigeons.
